data.name: Events.NoteOn.Description
data.value: Fires when a key is pressed in Control mode on a keyboard. Only subscribed keys are handled; every other key, and everything in Play mode, passes through.

data.name: Events.NoteOff.Description
data.value: Fires when a key is released on a keyboard. A release always goes where its press went.

data.name: Events.ControlChange.Description
data.value: Fires when a controller (knob, fader, pedal, CC) changes on a keyboard. Only the latest value is delivered.

data.name: Events.Device.Description
data.value: The keyboard to listen to. Leave empty for every keyboard registered.

data.name: Events.Note.Description
data.value: The key that triggers this event. Middle C is C4 (60).

data.name: Events.Controller.Description
data.value: The CC number (0-127), e.g. 64 for the sustain pedal.

data.name: Actions.SetMode.Description
data.value: Switches the router to Play or Control mode. In Play everything goes to the your app; in Control subscribed actions are executed.

data.name: Actions.SetMode.Target.Description
data.value: The mode to switch to, or Toggle to flip between Play and Control.

data.name: Actions.Routing.Description
data.value: Turns the router on or off. Off releases the keyboards so other apps can open them directly.

data.name: Actions.Routing.Switch.Description
data.value: Toggle, or always switch on or off.

data.name: Actions.SendCc.Description
data.value: Sends CC message to the router's output port.

data.name: Actions.SendNote.Description
data.value: Sends a note to the router's output port.

data.name: Actions.SendNote.Type.Description
data.value: A pressed note keeps sounding until a "Release" action is received.

data.name: Actions.SendNote.Velocity.Description
data.value: How hard the note is pressed, from 1 to 127.

data.name: Actions.SendNote.Duration.Description
data.value: How long the note stays pressed before it is released.

data.name: Actions.SendProgram.Description
data.value: Sends a Program Change to the router's output port.

data.name: Actions.Panic.Description
data.value: Silences stuck notes in the app connected to the router's output port.

data.name: Actions.Learn.Listening.Message
data.value: Press a key or move a control on a keyboard.

data.name: Actions.Learn.NoKeyboards
data.value: No keyboards are open to learn from

data.name: Actions.ExportCubase.Description
data.value: Writes the virtual device as a Cubase / Nuendo MIDI Remote script.

data.name: Actions.ExportCubase.ExportedDetail
data.value: Switch the Virtual Device on, then click Reload Scripts in the MIDI Remote tab: Cubase finds it by its MIDI ports. For the device to follow Cubase, set fader mappings to Jump and mute or solo buttons to Toggle in the Mapping Assistant.

data.name: Actions.ExportCubase.ExportedToFolder
data.value: Exported, but no Cubase or Nuendo was found

data.name: Editor.Status.DeleteHint
data.value: Select an element to delete it.

data.name: Editor.Status.Hint
data.value: Choose an element above, then press an empty cell to place it, or press an element to select it.

data.name: Editor.Status.MoveHint
data.value: Press the element to move, then the cell to move it to.

data.name: Editor.Status.MoveTarget
data.value: Now press the cell to move {label} to.

data.name: Editor.Status.Exported
data.value: Exported to {apps}. With the device switched on, click Reload Scripts in Cubase's MIDI Remote tab. In the Mapping Assistant, set faders to Jump and mute or solo buttons to Toggle, so the device follows Cubase.

data.name: Editor.Status.ExportedToFolder
data.value: Exported to {folder}. No Cubase or Nuendo Driver Scripts folder was found: copy its Local folder into that folder.

data.name: FolderViews.Mixer.Description
data.value: The virtual device as a mixer, with a power key: switched on, it has its own MIDI ports, and its buttons and faders follow what the DAW sends back.

data.name: Actions.ExportCubase.NoElementsDetail
data.value: Add buttons and faders on the Virtual Device page of MIDI Router.

data.name: Editor.Status.MoveTargetSelected
data.value: Press the cell to move the selected element to, or another element to move that one.

data.name: Editor.Status.Duplicate
data.value: {element} and {twin} both send {binding}: Cubase sees them as one control.

data.name: Actions.ExportCubase.ExportedToFolderDetail
data.value: Copy the Local folder from {folder} into the Driver Scripts folder. On macOS, Macro Deck also needs access to the Documents folder (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Files and Folders).

data.name: Editor.Status.Full
data.value: The device is full: Macro Deck can't draw more than this. Remove an element or use small buttons, which take the least.

data.name: ConfigFlow.StepDescriptionLoopback
data.value: Select the keyboards to route and the loopback port (loopMIDI, or a Windows MIDI Services loopback). In the target app, disable the hardware keyboard and enable loopback port instead.

data.name: ConfigFlow.StepDescriptionVirtual
data.value: Select the keyboards to route. The router creates a virtual port. In the target app, disable hardware keyboard and enable the router's virtual port.

data.name: ConfigFlow.InputDevices.Description
data.value: MIDI inputs for the router. Inputs that are not selected are never opened.

data.name: ConfigFlow.OutputDevice.DescriptionLoopback
data.value: This PC cannot create a virtual port for the router (it needs Windows MIDI Services): create one with loopMIDI or the Windows MIDI Services settings and select it here.

data.name: ConfigFlow.OutputDevice.DescriptionVirtual
data.value: The router's own virtual port is recommended.

data.name: ConfigFlow.OutputDevice.Virtual
data.value: Virtual port created by MIDI Router

data.name: ConfigFlow.VirtualPortName.Description
data.value: The name the target app shows for the plugin.

data.name: ConfigFlow.StartMode.Description
data.value: The mode the router is in when Macro Deck starts.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.StepDescription
data.value: In Play mode - no action executed; in Control mode subscribed keys will run their actions. Here you can dedicate the key or CC for switching between modes.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.NoteDescription
data.value: Pick a key you don't need for playing, e.g. the lowest A0 (21) or highest C8 (108).

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.ControllerDescription
data.value: 64 sustain, 66 sostenuto, 67 soft pedal. Counts as pressed from value 64.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.Listening
data.value: Listening: press the key or CC button on {device} you want as the shortcut. Click ✕ to stop.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.ActionHold
data.value: Control while held, back to Play on release

data.name: Issues.NotConfigured.Description
data.value: The router passes nothing through until you select at least one keyboard in its settings.

data.name: Issues.OutputFailed.Title
data.value: Output port '{port}' could not be opened

data.name: Issues.InputMissing.Description
data.value: The router opens it as soon as it is plugged in or wakes up.

data.name: Issues.InputBusy.Description
data.value: Another app holds the keyboard. Disable it in that app (for Dorico: Preferences > Play > MIDI Input Devices); the router retries by itself.

data.name: Issues.InputIsRouterOutput.Description
data.value: Reading the router's output back would create a feedback loop, so this input is ignored. Remove it from the keyboards.

data.name: Device.PowerFailed
data.value: The Virtual Device couldn't switch on

data.name: Device.NoMidiServices
data.value: It needs Windows MIDI Services to create its MIDI ports, and this PC doesn't have it. Install Windows MIDI Services, then switch the device on again.

data.name: Device.Unsupported
data.value: This system can't create MIDI ports for it.

data.name: Device.NameTaken
data.value: {name} is the name of the router's own port. Give the Virtual Device another name on its page.

data.name: Editor.Centered.Description
data.value: Rests in the middle and reads left and right, with a detent at the centre. Double-press it to centre it. For pan.
